summary: Registers an Enumservice for the Inter-Asterisk eXchange (IAX) protocol, following the guidelines in RFC 6117. This lets telephone numbers looked up through ENUM point to IAX endpoints.

eli5.summary: This adds one new entry to a phone-number directory, saying that a number can be reached using the IAX voice protocol.

questions: how do i point a phone number to an iax address
subtitle: Registering 'iax' so a telephone number can point to an Inter-Asterisk eXchange endpoint.

tldr.problem: ENUM turns telephone numbers into URIs through DNS, but there was no registered way to say that a number can be reached using the IAX protocol.
tldr.mechanism: The document registers the 'iax' Enumservice, a Protocol-Based type that maps E.164 numbers to IAX URIs, following the guidelines of RFC 6117.
tldr.outcome: A DNS record of the form E2U+iax can now point a number to an IAX destination, and clients selecting it must be able to speak IAX.

today: RFC 6315 is an Informational RFC that has not been obsoleted or updated. It is the registration document for the 'iax' Enumservice.

sections.title: ENUM and IAX
sections.content:
ENUM (RFC 6116) transforms E.164 telephone numbers into Uniform Resource Identifiers using the Domain Name System. IAX, the Inter-Asterisk eXchange protocol (RFC 5456), is an all-in-one protocol for handling multimedia in IP networks that combines control and media services in the same protocol.

This document registers an Enumservice for IAX according to the guidelines given in RFC 6117.
sections.eli5: ENUM is a phone book that turns phone numbers into internet addresses. IAX is one way to make a call, and this adds it to the book.

sections.title: The Registration
sections.content:
The registration is a template filled in with these values: class Protocol-Based, type iax, no subtype, URI scheme iax and usage COMMON. The Enumservice maps E.164 numbers to IAX URIs that identify resources capable of being contacted for a communication session using IAX.

A client selecting this NAPTR record needs to be able to support communication using the IAX protocol. The requesters are Ed Guy and Klaus Darilion, and the security field points to Section 4 of this document.
sections.eli5: The new entry says: 'if a number is listed this way, you need to know how to speak IAX to reach it'.

sections.title: Examples
sections.content:
The first example is a NAPTR record with service E2U+iax and the replacement iax:example.com/alice. It says the party at E.164 number +442079460148 can be contacted using IAX at domain example.com, where 'alice' identifies the called party, service or program.

The second uses an IPv6 address and a context: iax:[2001:db8::1]:4569/alice?friends. Here +442079460149 is reached over IAX at 2001:db8::1, port 4569, with called party 'alice' in the context (or user partition) 'friends'. The RFC stresses that the examples are only illustrative and do not limit how the Enumservice may be used.
sections.eli5: Each example is a phone-book line: 'for this number, call alice at this address using IAX'. The second one also says which group, called a context, to use.

sections.title: Security and DNS Considerations
sections.content:
The Enumservice adds no new security issues beyond those already present in ENUM, DNS and IAX, except that it provides for disclosure of information that may facilitate an attack or a violation of user privacy. The primary result of such exploits is unwanted communications; see RFC 3833. Use of DNSSEC (RFC 4033) is recommended, and Section 7 of RFC 6116 covers security considerations that apply to all Enumservices.

On the DNS side, misconfiguration or delays in zone changes can cause call loops, perhaps across different protocols or networks. Implementations should detect such loops without interrupting other services, including SIP-based, IAX-based and DNS itself.
sections.eli5: Anyone who can read the phone book could learn how to reach people, which might bring unwanted calls. Mistakes in the book can also make calls go round in circles, so programs should notice that.
